captures.description: Lexically captured values, distinct from source formal parameters.

receiver.description: Implicit source instance receiver, distinct from formal parameters and lexical captures.

returnKind.description: Immediate source invocation return. Void has no returned value; Task/Promise handles remain values even when eventual completion has no value. Omission leaves the return kind unresolved. Constructors require separate allocation semantics, not an inferred void invocation result.

mode.description: Variable binding mode: value copies the variable value (including an object reference, without copying the object); reference aliases its variable cell; unresolved establishes neither. Does not infer mutation, scheduling or invocation policy.

captureBindings.description: Actual lexical origins for a bound invocation. This does not itself establish callback scheduling or invocation policy.

receiver.description: Caller-owned instance receiver value; source syntax alone does not establish a callee or mutable alias effects.

waitsFor.description: Source call waiting boundary. None starts local asynchronous work without awaiting its completion; omission preserves legacy return traversal. Does not establish scheduler, synchronous prefix or interleaving.

associationOwners.description: Catalogue owners whose related facts are selected. Omission defaults to explicit records-query ids; pagination preserves the original selection.

trigger.description: Source registration kind. Omission preserves legacy REST entry semantics; non-REST bindings require their own protocol and declared address.

mode.description: Source-established write intent; unknown retains a proven write call and acknowledgement without guessing insert/update/replace/upsert/delete semantics. Unknown requires an explicit gap.

targetEntry.description: Known provider entry at the target component. Distinct caller_construction and source_declared provider contracts require identical established HTTP/HTTPS/gRPC protocol, method and path. Source address correspondence does not prove payload compatibility or deployed version correspondence.

contract.description: Contract describing the actual caller or consumer values. A linked provider entry may expose its own separate source-declared contract.
